title: Gateway burst-window parsing regression caused 429 wave — follow-up & remediation
creator: Alicia Romero
description: Summary: On 2026-02-25 15:12 UTC a configuration parsing change deployed to the API gateway caused the per-tenant burst window field (burst_window_ms) to be interpreted as seconds instead of milliseconds. This produced a 1000x reduction in effective burst window for many customers, rapidly triggering quota enforcement and producing a sustained 429 storm across multiple regions for ~45 minutes. The incident impacted request success rates for hosted API customers and triggered automated retries that amplified load on internal services.
timeline: 2026-02-25 14:55 UTC: Config rollout (gateway-config service v3.12.0) begins in canary region us-west-2-canary
2026-02-25 15:10 UTC: Error budget alarms fire for gateway rate-limiter; initial spike in 429s observed in canary
2026-02-25 15:12 UTC: Config rollout continues to prod regions (automation mis-evaluated canary health)
2026-02-25 15:18 UTC: Pager escalations to on-call infra and runtime teams; dashboards show increase in 429 rate and end-to-end latency
2026-02-25 15:25 UTC: Emergency rollback of gateway-config to v3.11.4 initiated (rollback completed by 15:32 UTC)
2026-02-25 15:35 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: rate-limiter soft-fail mode (accept with warning) for affected tenants to reduce client-side retries
2026-02-25 16:00 UTC: Traffic normalizes; follow-up incident bridge opened to collect data and plan remediation
root_causes: Regression in config parser: change in config schema validation accidentally converted numeric ms field to seconds when target field absent
Insufficient canary gating: our canary health check criteria did not surface the 429 pattern (we only monitored CPU and memory, not quota/error rate)
Missing config compatibility unit tests covering legacy format expectations across versions
Retry amplification: clients immediately retried on 429 without backoff causing secondary load spike
No pre-deploy contract checks between gateway-config and rate-limiter about window units
impact_summary: ~45 minute global impact window (15:12–16:00 UTC) with highest severity between 15:18–15:35 UTC
~18% of production requests returned 429s at peak across hosted API; top 25 customers saw elevated error rates
Operational load: multiple on-call teams engaged for bridge and rollback; two customer support escalations logged
No evidence of data loss or security compromise
immediate_mitigations: Rollback gateway-config to last known-good v3.11.4
Enable rate-limiter soft-fail mode to accept requests with diagnostic header for 30 minutes to reduce retries
Temporarily increase quota thresholds for top affected tenants while monitoring metrics
Throttle internal retryers (internal SDKs) to add jitter and exponential backoff
long_term_action_items: (Owner: Marcus Lin) Add strict schema validation and backwards compatibility tests for gateway-config parsing; ensure unit tests cover ms<->s conversions — due 2026-03-12
(Owner: Priya Nair) Expand canary gating criteria to include SLOs: 5xx/4xx rate, 429 rate, and request success percent — due 2026-03-19
(Owner: Rafael Gomez) Implement pre-deploy contract checks that validate expected units for rate-limiter config keys and fail fast in CI — due 2026-03-16
(Owner: Emma Zhao) Add a quota-enforcer dry-run mode for config changes with a shadow evaluation to detect behavior changes before rollout — due 2026-04-02
(Owner: Support) Update customer retry guidance and SDKs to implement backoff and jitter by default; include emergency throttle handling — due 2026-03-30
(Owner: Observability) Create a dedicated 429 storm dashboard and automated alerting playbook with paging thresholds and runbook links — due 2026-03-09
(Owner: Security) Review RBAC for config rollout automation and add an audit checkpoint for config schema changes — due 2026-03-22
notes_and_discussions: 2026-02-26: Postmortem writeup draft completed by Alicia; initial review requested from runtime and QA teams
2026-03-01: Design review with Priya and Rafael — agreed to add contract checks into the CI pipeline and to expand canary metrics
2026-03-04: Ops runbook updated with new emergency soft-fail toggle and instructions for setting tenant-level temporary quotas
2026-03-08: Engineering review: proposal to add a lightweight schema linter in pre-commit to catch ms vs s errors; Marcus to prototype
2026-03-10: Customer success confirmed two enterprise customers were notified with incident summary and offered post-incident syncs
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests added that assert burst_window_ms is parsed and stored in milliseconds across versions
CI gate fails if any config change modifies recognized units for existing keys
New canary gating monitors active and producing alerts in next deploy cycle
429 storm dashboard visible in Console with runbook links and paging thresholds
Retry behavior in SDKs updated and released (minor version) to reduce amplification risk
owner_notes: Marcus Lin: Prioritizing schema tests and CI contract checks this sprint. Prototype for pre-commit linter planned by 2026-03-05.
Priya Nair: Canary gating change requires small infra work to publish 429-rate metric to canary dashboards; will coordinate with Observability team.
Rafael Gomez: Contract check will be implemented as a standalone GitHub Action to allow reuse across repos.
